items.review_rationale: Read contravariance as ordinary covariance from the opposite category, including reversal of arrow direction and corresponding composition without introducing a second notion of functor.

references.context: The output morphism in D goes from the image of the original target to the image of its source.

references.disposition: Opposite-category formulation entails reversed composition and preservation of identities in the appropriate order.

items.review_rationale: Read opposite category with identical object collection, all hom-set directions reversed, and reversed composition preserving the categorical identity and associativity laws.

references.context: For each pair X,Y, the hom-set of the opposite category is the reversed-direction hom-set of C.
If reversed arrows compose in C^op, their composite corresponds to the reversed order of the underlying C-composition.

references.disposition: The opposite category does not replace or dualize the objects themselves, only the morphisms and composition order.

items.review_rationale: Read the contravariant representable presheaf h_U with values Hom_C(X,U) and restriction by precomposition, preserving fixed representing object U and the arrow direction.

references.context: Morphisms in C from varying source X to fixed representing target U.
Given g:Y→X, take f:X→U to f∘g:Y→U, providing h_U(X)→h_U(Y).

references.disposition: The fixed object U is in the target slot of Hom_C(X,U); covariant Hom_C(U,−) is a different represented functor.
